title: Stable core
description: What every client and daemon version must keep reading: the hello, the daemon's version and build kind it carries, the request to exit, and the record that names the daemon's channel. Definitions marked x-stableCore never change except by a new optional property, whatever the contract version, and every object here accepts properties it does not know. The stable core holds no enum, since a value added later could not be read by an older version: a field that names one of a set is a plain string whose x-readAs names the enum it is read as, and x-unknownReadsAs the value a reader takes for a string it does not know.

HelloStart.description: The client's first message on a connection: a fresh nonce and who it is. Nothing else may be sent before the hello finishes.

clientNonce.description: A fresh random value: 32 to 256 hex digits, lowercase. The daemon closes the connection on any other.

clientName.description: 1 to 200 characters; the daemon closes the connection on any other. Where the client runs, as people read it in the daemon's log, in a busy brick's message and in a question: "EVƎ C (VS Code)", "ev3 c run (terminal)".

clientKind.description: Who the client is, one of ClientKind. A kind the daemon does not know reads as mcp, the least privileged: it is never asked a person's question and cannot ask the daemon to exit.

contractVersion.description: The contract version the client was built with.

buildKind.description: One of BuildKind. A build kind the daemon does not know reads as release, so it never counts as a development build that replaces a release daemon.

HelloChallenge.description: The daemon's answer to hello/start: its own nonce and its proof over both nonces. A client that cannot verify the proof is talking to something else and closes the connection.

daemonNonce.description: A fresh random value, lowercase hex.

daemonProof.description: HMAC-SHA256 with the user's key over "daemon\n<clientNonce>\n<daemonNonce>", lowercase hex.

HelloFinish.description: The client's proof. The daemon accepts the connection, or closes it.

clientProof.description: HMAC-SHA256 with the user's key over "client\n<clientNonce>\n<daemonNonce>", lowercase hex.

HelloAccepted.description: Who the daemon is, once both sides have proved they hold the user's key. A client whose contract version differs says so and stops instead of misbehaving.

buildKind.description: One of BuildKind; a build kind the client does not know reads as release.

buildId.description: SHA-256 of the daemon's own executable, lowercase hex, computed when it started.

mode.description: One of DaemonMode; a mode the client does not know reads as hardware, since the daemon may then touch real bricks.

state.description: One of DaemonState. Absent, or a state the client does not know, reads as serving.

transports.description: Transports the daemon could load, for a client to notice a degraded one.

DaemonExitParams.description: Ask the daemon to end. The daemon judges the request from the asking client's hello: a newer release client, or a development client meeting a release daemon, replaces it once no write is in progress. Any other request is a restart, which runs only after a person said yes.

accepted.description: The daemon ends as soon as no write is in progress.

reason.description: Why it refused, ready to show.

ChannelRecord.description: channel.json, which only the daemon holding the single-instance lock writes and removes on a clean exit. A client connects only to the path recorded here and never computes it itself.

path.description: The full named pipe path on Windows, the full unix socket path on Linux.
